- If sentiment is positive (≥0.20) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to reflect bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.20), model often overestimates near-term upside — reduce forecast early to avoid overcorrection.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots — cap forecast growth to 3–5% per day post-spike.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon — add 2–4% buffer to forecast mean if recent 7-day average is rising.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and history shows volatility, model tends to smooth too much — introduce 1–2% volatility bump in forecast tail.  
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model often ignores it — reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 5 days.
